claims.statement: Installing, reloading and uninstalling a desktop component are filesystem operations on a plugin root — dropping a directory installs it, editing its plugin.json or entry module reloads it, deleting the directory uninstalls it — and none of the three needs a panel restart, a command or a registry entry.

The plugin root list is resolved once at boot as the built-in root dist/renderer/cards followed by config.plugins.dir or, when that config value is the empty string, userData/plugins; the built-in root being first is what makes built-in components win id conflicts, and changing the configured directory requires a restart.

watchPluginRoots creates each plugin root with fs.mkdirSync(dir, { recursive: true }) before installing a recursive fs.watch on it, and merges every event into a single callback that fires once after a settle window defaulting to 300 ms; the offline watcher test overrides that window with settleMs 40.

A plugin root that cannot be created or watched is skipped silently, and nothing rescans plugin roots periodically — the 1 Hz snapshot re-serves the cached listing from PluginHostService.info() — so a directory dropped into an unwatched root is only noticed by an explicit rescan() or a panel restart.

rescan() diffs asset fingerprints per plugin id: a new id is installed at revision 1, a changed fingerprint unloads the existing instance (calling dispose) and then installs a fresh one with the revision incremented, a disappeared id is unloaded and its generation record dropped, and an unchanged fingerprint does no work at all.

The asset fingerprint is the serialized parsed manifest plus the entry file's mtimeMs and size, so an edit that the manifest parser discards (reformatting, an unknown key) and an edit to any file other than the entry module produce a rescan but no reload and no plugins/changed event.

PluginInfo.entry is emitted as deck-plugin://<id>/<entry>?v=<revision>, a protocol URL that is unique per asset generation; a missing entry asset instead produces status error with an empty entry string.

The ?v=<revision> query string is the mechanism that defeats the renderer's ESM module cache: a dynamic import is cached by module specifier, cache-control no-store on the asset response does not affect that cache, and only a URL that has never been imported causes the module to be fetched and evaluated again on reload.

The renderer decides a reload purely by comparing info.entry with the entry URL the current mount was based on: a different URL unmounts and remounts the component, and because the failure ledger is also keyed by the entry URL a new revision retries immediately instead of waiting out the 30 s cooldown.

When an import throws or the imported module exports no callable mount, mountOne records the failure in a ledger keyed by the entry URL, notifies plugin-load-failed, draws nothing, and does not retry that same URL for 30 s (FAIL_RETRY_MS).

In-flight loads are guarded by a per-plugin generation token re-checked after the await import, so a load that finishes after its component was unmounted or replaced is discarded rather than resurrecting the component; the token is per plugin because a single global counter made concurrently imported cards invalidate each other.

On a successful load the renderer appends a container div.deck-plugin (class and data-plugin-id) to the element named by manifest.mount or to document.body when that id is absent or not found, hands the module a view trimmed to the manifest's capabilities, calls mount(host), records plugin-mounted, and re-declares hotzones because the DOM changed.
A mount hook that throws removes the container that was just appended, records plugin-mount-failed in the same cooldown ledger, and leaves no partially drawn component on screen.

A throwing update is reported as plugin-update-failed and leaves the component mounted; because the renderer stores the new trimmed view and view key before invoking update, the failed state is not retried until the trimmed view changes again.

Removal is driven by the listing: every mounted component whose id is not in the status ok set is unmounted by bumping its generation token, clearing its failure ledger entry, calling unmount() inside a try/catch and removing the host-owned container, after which hotzones are re-declared so the freed pixels return to pass-through instead of leaving a dead clickable rectangle.

A plugin directory whose manifest is invalid or missing produces no instance and is listed under a fallback id derived from the directory name (broken when nothing survives), while a valid manifest whose entry asset is missing is listed as status error with an empty entry and the reason 入口资产不存在: …; neither is ever mounted, so both are silent degradations with no dialog.

Duplicate ids are resolved by scan order: valid manifests claim their id first with the earliest root winning and the loser warned about on the console but omitted from the listing, and a broken directory's fallback id enters the listing only while that id is still free.

A plugin instance whose ready() throws synchronously is deleted from the live map, which also removes its protocol asset root, so the component's entry URL becomes a 404 while the listing still reports status ok and the page records a load failure instead; a rejected promise returned by ready is not caught because the call is discarded with void.

The renderer-side hot-plug steps are observable in the evidence log through the renderer's notify channel — plugins-changed, plugin-mounted, plugin-load-failed, plugin-mount-failed, plugin-update-failed — plus whatever the component reports itself (for example hello-mounted), whereas the main-process scan, install, unload and dispose write nothing to that log and only console.warn with the deck-plugins: prefix.

There is no unmount event in the evidence log: an uninstall is observable only through the next hotzones record no longer containing the component's card id, which is exactly how the acceptance battery proves the card left the clickable map.

Acceptance phase P11 asserts the four hot-plug steps without a restart: install requires plugin-mounted hello, the component's own hello-mounted and a hello-card hotzone; editing card.js requires a second plugin-mounted for the same id within 15 s; uninstall requires hello-card to disappear from the hotzones; reinstall requires plugin-mounted and the hotzone again — and the phase counts boot records to prove the panel never restarted.

plugins/changed is pushed out of band from the 1 Hz snapshot so a hot-plug is visible immediately, and the page's handler applies the new list against the snapshot it already holds rather than asking the kernel again; on a cold start the components instead arrive through the first panel/snapshot because the host performs its first scan during construction.

Mount order is listing order: the listing is sorted by order ascending with id as tie-break and the page mounts components in that sequence, so order decides the DOM append order of body-appended containers; the built-in cards declare 10/20/30/50, and an undeclared order defaults to DEFAULT_PLUGIN_ORDER 1000.

A desktop component is only clickable when its own element carries the shared card class and an id, because the hotzone declaration is derived from .card elements; a component that skips it still renders but its pixels stay inside the window's pass-through region.

Copying a component in file by file is not atomic from the host's point of view: a rescan landing between two files can see a valid manifest whose entry is not written yet and list it as status error, which a later filesystem event self-heals; the settle window is what normally merges the individual file copies into a single rescan.

The sample component samples/hello-plugin declares capabilities [clock] and order 900 and reports hello-mounted from its mount hook, which is what lets acceptance prove the imported module actually ran rather than merely being delivered to the page.

Offline coverage drives the rescan explicitly with watch: false for determinism, with a single test opting into a real watcher with a 40 ms settle window; the renderer plugin runtime has no unit test, so mount, hotzone and reload behaviour is asserted only from a running panel by the acceptance battery.
